name: context-heat
description: Your editor gets hot as your Claude Code context window fills up.

commands.title: Context Heat: Install or Update Statusline Bridge

contextHeat.enabled.description: Heat the UI as the Claude Code context window fills.

enumDescriptions: Share of conversation tokens touching files you are still working on.

contextHeat.show.markdownDescription:
Which numbers appear in the status bar. With just `context` it reads `🔥🔥 74%`; add more and they get labelled: `🔥🔥 ctx 74% · 5h 34% · 7d 77% · fcs 58%`.

`focus` is a share of the **conversation**, not of the context window — they are not parts of one whole.

The tooltip always shows everything available.

contextHeat.showPercentage.description: Show the numeric percentage next to the flames.

contextHeat.animate.description: Flicker the status bar flames in the hottest bands.

contextHeat.hideWhenCold.description: Hide the status bar item entirely below the first threshold.

enumDescriptions: Follow whichever of the three is highest.
contextHeat.heatFrom.markdownDescription:
Which number drives the colour and flames.

This is independent of `#contextHeat.show#` — the temperature can follow a number the status bar is not displaying. If Claude Code does not report the chosen limit, it falls back to the context window rather than going cold.

enumDescriptions: Share of the whole context window. This is the number Claude Code itself reports.
Share of the context you get before auto-compact fires. Reaches 100% when you are about to be compacted.
contextHeat.contextBasis.markdownDescription:
What the context percentage is measured against.

This is why Context Heat and ccstatusline can disagree: ccstatusline divides by a usable window, so 32% of a 1M window reads as 40% there. Neither is wrong — they answer different questions. Use `untilCompact` to match it.

contextHeat.compactAtPercent.markdownDescription: What percentage of the window auto-compact fires at. Only used when `#contextHeat.contextBasis#` is `untilCompact`.

contextHeat.thresholds.markdownDescription:
Context percentage at which each band begins.

`blazing` is "on fire" — the normal maximum heat. `critical` and `meltdown` escalate above it.

Setting one value moves the defaults below it out of the way, so `{ "blazing": 55 }` alone works.

critical.description: Past maximum. Faster, harsher, shouts COMPACT.

enumDescriptions: Write colors to this folder's .vscode/settings.json. Each window heats independently.
Write colors to your user settings. Every window heats together.
Never write colors. Status bar indicator only.

contextHeat.gradient.markdownDescription:
Ramp the tint down the window: faint at the title bar, full strength at the status bar. VS Code has no real gradient, so this uses alpha per surface, which composites over your theme and works in light and dark.

Turn off for a flat tint on every surface.

contextHeat.surfaces.markdownDescription:
Which chrome surfaces heat up, listed top to bottom. Enable more of them for a smoother gradient.

`windowBorder` needs `window.titleBarStyle` set to `custom`.

contextHeat.focusRecentFraction.description: What counts as "now" for focus: the fraction of the conversation, from the end, whose files define your current working set.

contextHeat.checkBridge.description: On startup, check whether the statusline bridge is installed and up to date, and offer to fix it.

contextHeat.bridgeDirectory.description: Directory the statusline bridge writes to. Defaults to ~/.claude/context-heat.

contextHeat.forgetEndedAfterSeconds.description: How long to keep showing a session's last reading after its process has exited. Running sessions are never forgotten, however long they sit idle.

contextHeat.pruneAfterDays.description: Delete bridge files untouched for this many days, at startup.

steps.title: Install the bridge
steps.description:
Put the bridge script in ~/.claude and point Claude Code at it.
[Install the bridge](command:contextHeat.installBridge)

steps.title: Restart Claude Code
steps.description: Claude Code reads statusLine at startup, so restart it for the bridge to take effect.

steps.title: See it heat up
steps.description:
You cannot reach 90% on demand, so turn the dial by hand.
[Simulate a temperature](command:contextHeat.simulate)

steps.title: Choose what it shows
steps.description:
Pick which numbers appear, what drives the colour, and which parts of the editor tint.
[Open settings](command:workbench.action.openSettings?%22contextHeat%22)
